name: ChristopherKahler/paul + seed — PAUL (1K Stars) + SEED (281 Stars); Plan-Apply-Unify Loop; Acceptance-Criteria-First Development
hook: PAUL (Plan-Apply-Unify Loop) enforces a strict Plan→Apply→Unify cycle where every work unit closes with a UNIFY step that reconciles what was planned vs what happened — blocking 'context rot' as sessions fill. Acceptance criteria are first-class citizens, not afterthoughts. Companion SEED interviews requirements via 8–10 pointed questions (type-aware guided exploration), then packages the output into a spec Claude hands directly to PAUL. @charlieautomates called the combo 'The Claude Code Meta Nobody's Talking About.' PAUL: 1K stars, MIT; SEED: 281 stars; both free on npm.

name: JuliusBrussee/caveman — 92.3K Stars; Day 4; 65% Fewer Output Tokens; Caveman-Speak, Full Accuracy
hook: Compresses agent responses into terse caveman-speak without losing any technical accuracy — code, commands, and error messages remain byte-for-byte exact, only the prose is stripped. Benchmarked at 65% average output token reduction (range 22–87% across 1,200 test scenarios). Output tokens are typically 1–2% of a Claude Code bill, so the gains are largest for output-heavy automation. 92.3K stars, 5.2K forks. With Opus 5's 128K output cap, long agentic sessions can accumulate significant output costs — caveman's compression keeps those predictable.
recurring_note: ↑ Day 4 — 92.3K stars; output-cost control increasingly relevant with Opus 5's high output cap

name: thedotmack/claude-mem — 88.3K Stars; Day 4; Persistent Memory Across Sessions; 5 Hooks + SQLite + Chroma
hook: Solves session amnesia with five lifecycle hooks (SessionStart, PostToolUse, Stop, UserPromptSubmit, SessionEnd) that capture every tool use, file read, and edit; a local Bun worker compresses observations via Claude Agent SDK and stores them in SQLite with full-text search and Chroma for hybrid semantic/keyword retrieval. name: anthropics/ralph-wiggum — Official Anthropic Loop Plugin; 139K Stars; Day 3; Stop Hook Keeps Claude Working Until Done
hook: Ralph Wiggum is the official Anthropic autonomous-loop plugin inside the claude-code repo: a Stop hook blocks Claude's exit, re-injects the original prompt, and loops until Claude outputs a configurable completion phrase (e.g., `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>`) or hits `--max-iterations`. Concrete benefit: you can hand it a greenfield REST API spec and walk away — Claude reads its own git history and file output each iteration to improve, catches its own test failures, and only stops when done. 139K stars, 22.3K forks. With Opus 5's depth-3 subagents now the default, ralph-wiggum loops can now coordinate three-tier orchestration trees per iteration.
